title: How to Choose a Builder in Chennai: Checks, Contract, Red Flags

seo.metaTitle: How to Choose a Builder in Chennai: Checklist | Hunter Property
seo.metaDescription: A practical checklist for choosing a builder in Chennai: which old work to inspect, the paperwork to check, what the agreement must name and the red flags.

excerpt: Photographs of finished houses tell you little. This checklist shows how to judge a Chennai builder by two-year-old work, basic paperwork, the construction agreement and one unscripted reference.

faqs.question: What should I look at when visiting a builder’s completed house?
faqs.answer: Four things that fail first: bathroom ceilings on the floor below a wet area, the junction where the parapet meets the terrace slab, door frames in rooms that get afternoon sun, and grout lines in the kitchen.

faqs.question: Why visit a house built two years ago rather than a new one?
faqs.answer: Tiles look good on handover day whatever sits under them, and waterproofing can take eighteen months to fail. A two-year-old house shows whether the build was sequenced properly.

faqs.question: What are the red flags when choosing a builder?
faqs.answer: A quote with no bill of quantities, reluctance to share addresses of completed projects, a large upfront payment before work starts, no written timeline, and a rate far below the market. Two of these together is a reason to keep looking.

faqs.question: How do I find a reference the builder did not choose?
faqs.answer: Talk to a neighbour at the site you visit; it usually takes one conversation. Ask what slipped on the project and whether it was fixed or argued about.

faqs.question: What should the agreement name instead of “good quality materials”?
faqs.answer: The cement brand, steel grade, a tile allowance per sq ft and a sanitaryware budget, together with a stage-linked payment schedule and a defect liability period in writing.
